transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well… I guess I’m here because I just haven’t been myself since my friend from choir passed away so suddenly. We did so much together through church, and it shook me more than I expected. Since then, little things that I used to handle just fine feel like too much.

I mean, I’ll be looking at something simple like the potluck list, just names and casseroles and who’s bringing what, and I’ll start crying. Or someone will call me about planning something, the kind of calls I used to take without even thinking, and I get all worked up and flustered. And I’ve even started missing church planning things—meetings and responsibilities I never would have missed before. That’s not like me at all.
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things the way you used to, like activities or events you used to look forward to?

I’m not sure I’d put it exactly that way. I mean… I still care about the things I used to care about, if that makes sense. Church and choir and the ladies there, those still matter to me. I wouldn’t say I don’t enjoy anything anymore.

It’s more that when something reminds me of my friend, or when an event feels like it should include her, it kind of takes the wind out of me. So I might still want to go, or I might think, “Oh, that’ll be nice,” and then I get there and it feels different. But I don’t know that I’ve noticed a complete loss of enjoyment, no. It’s just… everything feels tangled up with missing her right now.
Do you find yourself feeling down or sad even when you’re not thinking about your friend or situations that remind you of her?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I do have sad moments, but when I try to think about it, it’s hard to separate it out from her, because so much of my week seems to have some little connection to her or to church or choir. Even things that don’t seem like they would remind me of her can sort of lead back there in my mind.

So… I wouldn’t say I’m just sad all the time for no reason, if that’s what you mean. It feels more like it comes in waves, and a lot of the time there’s something that sets it off, even if I don’t realize it right away. But I don’t know that I’ve paid close enough attention to say for certain.
Can you think of a time recently when you felt down or sad when you weren’t thinking about your friend or anything related to her or the church?

I’m trying to think of one, and honestly… most of the times I can point to, it does seem to circle back to her somehow. Like I’ll tell myself, “Oh, I’m just having a bad morning,” but then I realize I was looking at the potluck list and her name wasn’t there, or someone called me about something we always used to do together, and suddenly I’m crying or all worked up.

It’s not so much that I’m sitting around feeling sad out of nowhere, at least not that I can clearly say. It’s more that ever since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself. Things I used to handle without batting an eye—church planning calls, choir things, organizing who’s bringing what—now they feel overwhelming, and sometimes I avoid them or miss things I never would’ve missed before. So I guess I can’t really think of a clean example where it had nothing to do with her or church. It all feels tangled together.
How long has it been since your friend passed away?

It’s been just about a month now. It still feels strange saying that, because in my head it’s like it just happened, but then I look at the calendar and it’s been weeks already.

She died so suddenly, and really, that’s when I started falling apart with all the church planning things. Before that I was managing, you know, keeping up with the calls and the lists and the choir things, but after she was gone… it all just started feeling like too much.
Can you think of any time in the past two weeks when you felt down, overwhelmed, or unable to cope, when there wasn’t a direct reminder of your friend or something related to church or choir?

I’m trying to think, and I don’t know that I can separate it that neatly. In the past two weeks, the times I’ve felt really down or like I couldn’t cope, there usually was something tied to her, even if it seemed small at first.

Like the potluck lists… I know that probably sounds silly, but I’ll be looking at who’s bringing what, and then I notice her name isn’t there, or I think of how she would’ve called me about it, and I just start crying. Or with the planning calls, things I used to handle without even thinking—just making a few calls, checking on choir things, keeping track of details—now I get all worked up. I’ll put it off, or I’ll miss something I never would’ve missed before.

So if you’re asking whether I’ve felt overwhelmed with no reminder at all, I honestly can’t think of a clear example. It’s more like ever since she passed so suddenly, I just haven’t been myself, and all these church and choir things that used to feel normal now set me off.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms are closely tied to the recent loss of her friend, with sadness and difficulty coping primarily linked to reminders of the deceased. These symptoms began approximately one month ago and are specifically connected to the stressor rather than being prolonged or occurring without triggers. This supports the diagnosis of Adjustment Disorder with Depressed Mood (F43.22). Major Depressive Disorder (F32.x) is less likely due to the time frame, lack of pervasive anhedonia, and the clear contextual link to a recent bereavement.
